units.function: Embedded-PostgreSQL integration and opt-in benchmark coverage for batched company import writes, imported-work counts, inbox suppression and chunk rollback.
units.dependencyDirection: Synthetic portability bundles drive the real companyPortabilityService; a monkey-patched Drizzle db/transaction counts insert calls while issue/work-product services verify downstream projections.
units.keyDataModels: Schema-v6 inline bundle, issues/comments/documents, issue inbox archive, work products, contiguous issue identifiers and per-table insert counts.
units.lifecycle: Build/import a new company bundle, batch entity writes, seed imported issues out of the importing user's inbox, roll back a two-chunk work-product insert on later failure and optionally benchmark 500 issues.
units.testAssessment: The tests are strong on statement-count regression, persisted shape, a focused transaction rollback and post-import inbox UX. The approved isolated run reported the whole file skipped: four tests skipped, including the intentionally opt-in benchmark, because this host's embedded-PostgreSQL support was unavailable; no pass is claimed. Coverage does not prove whole-import atomicity, parser/ZIP limits, memory, cancellation/progress, concurrency, retry/idempotency, crash recovery, lock/deadlock behavior or source-authorship fidelity.
units.designRationale: Replace one-row-per-statement imports with bounded chunks while preventing a migrated workspace from flooding the importing user's active inbox.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs large governed organization/data migrations that are efficient, restartable, attributable and provenance preserving across managed-cloud and self-hosted deployments.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the real-database statement-count guard, chunk-boundary rollback fixture, imported-count verification and opt-in scale benchmark. Add whole-job durable checkpoints, canonical content digest/idempotency, cancellation, bounded parsing/resources, concurrent-import exclusion, outbox progress and original-author/source assertions.
units.responsibilityConflict: The fixture confirms imported user-authored comments are intentionally re-attributed to the importing board user. That improves inbox semantics by rewriting authorship, but Company OS must keep source author identity/provenance separate from the accountable human who approved or executed import.
evidence: 075951f6bde525de0ff5b0daad216f60c3083ded Fix import completion UX: inbox flood, false-failure message, stale company list (#10538)
2026-08-18 approved isolated verbose Vitest: 1 file / 4 tests skipped; no passing claim

units.function: Two shared constants for the company-import relative route and assembled HTTP API path.
units.dependencyDirection: A server route-name constant is assembled into a browser-facing /api/companies/import path and imported by transport consumers.
units.keyDataModels: Literal /import relative path and /api/companies/import absolute application path.
units.lifecycle: Compile-time string reuse only; there is no request, schema, versioning, deprecation or compatibility lifecycle.
units.testAssessment: No dedicated test is warranted for the two literal constants, but no contract test verifies server registration/client generation or version compatibility either.
units.designRationale: Avoid duplicated route strings drifting across server and UI.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs one canonical transport specification for independent Web, API clients and deployment profiles without leaking HTTP details into core/application.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY. Keep route naming in an API adapter or generated OpenAPI client and prove it with compatibility tests; core commands/events and Connector SDK must remain independent of HTTP path constants.
units.responsibilityConflict: None in the constant itself, but it expresses no identity, authority, approval, idempotency, data contract or evidence requirements for the high-risk import operation.
